Clients filter the slashed validators immediately at the fork in the first epoch of the fork (use Gloas logic by version of the state instead of using the pre-lookahead). 2. Clients do not filter the slashed validators at fork+1, when computing the lookahead for fork + 2. I don't know if we have fork tests for either of these behaviors spectests I mean it's part of `state_transition` and we have spec tests, I don't understand how that can happen, the implementation of this is trivial the worst case is probably clients serving stale/wrong duties if they use separate caches for that validator lookahead isn’t a new concept we added that in fulu Potuz is going to hide a lookahead bug in pyrsm just to prove y'all wrong 😁 what does this have to do with it? upgrade at the fork is the special thing. If clients call an update lookahead for Gloas right at the fork, then the next lookahead will be just wrong why does everything I ask for need to be so controversial? I just asked for a test, it should be a nobrainer that testing scenarios is always better than just assuming the implementation is trivial and won't be flawed I'm reviewing this exact code path in Prysm cause I suspected that I introduced the bug 1) above I agree with you that we should a test for this. But an e2e (devnet, diamond) test. we did test this on devnet-6 already, and yes we should test this, but if there are bugs due to this I wouldn't be worried about the change itself but rather some more fundamental issue with the client design or the spec tests/specs in general it's probably mostly worth to look at how you serve duties and how the validator client caches them, I suspect this will likely be source of issues if any this has nothing to do with duties in my concern. My concern is an actual consensus bug if the shuffling at the fork would point for the lookahead to have slashed validators in the first two epochs after Gloas and clients treating them differently, both epoch transitions last Fulu -> First Gloas and First Gloas -> Second Gloas are my worry and I think we should have tests for. I did audit Prysm and Prysm seems fine on both epoch transitions AFAICT I do not think devnet 6 forked with enough slashed validators to guaratee slashed validators in the first 2 epochs post Gloas? This is kinda crazy to test on devnet, needs to be Kurtosis or a spectest why do you wanna specifically test this on the devnet? shouldn't we just add more spec tests for this? eg For 1) a Fork spectest testvector with upgrade_to_gloas with prepared tons of slashed validators and check that there are slashed validators in the first two epochs of the lookahead For 2) an epoch transition on Gloas where the pre-state has slashed validators in the lookahead (this can happen in the first couple of epochs or after a slashing) and the second half of the lookahead does not have any after processing the epoch. excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Well, there are a gazillion bugs that can happen here:
1. Clients filter the slashed validators immediately at the fork in the first epoch of the fork (use Gloas logic by version of the state instead of using the pre-lookahead). 
2. Clients do not filter the slashed validators at fork+1, when computing the lookahead for fork + 2.
